source_caption:
Confession: I don’t usually watch anime, but this one hit me like a train I never saw coming.

Grave of the Fireflies is one of the most heartbreaking war films ever made, animated or not. It follows a young boy and his little sister trying to survive after their city is destroyed in WWII.  The story is personal , painfully personal. The writer, Akiyuki Nosaka, lived through WWII. During the war, he lost his little sister to malnutrition because he couldn’t save her. He carried that guilt his whole life. So he wrote this story as a confession, apology, and farewell that he never got to say in reality. He once said writing it hurt him , but not writing it would’ve hurt more. Every tear, every moment of hopelessness in this film comes from real memory… not imagination.

source_details.synopsis: Grave of the Fireflies (火垂るの墓, Hotaru no Haka) is a live-action TV drama adaptation of Grave of the Fireflies, made by NTV in Japan. It was produced in commemoration of the 60th anniversary of the end of World War II. The drama aired on November 1, 2005. Like the anime, the live-action version of Grave of the Fireflies focuses on two siblings, Seita and Setsuko, struggling to survive the final days of the war in Kobe, Japan. Unlike the animated version, it tells the story from the point of view of their cousin and also illustrates the war changing a kind lady into a hard-hearted woman.
